entry.title: Go Security Team Advises on Mitigating CVE-2026-98432 Linux Kernel Flaw
entry.content:

The Go Security Team has issued guidance regarding CVE-2026-98432, a critical use-after-free vulnerability affecting IPv4 TCP connection handling in the Linux kernel that can allow remote code execution when Multipath TCP listeners are exposed. While upgrading to a patched kernel remains the definitive fix, Go 1.24 and later versions enable Multipath TCP by default for listen sockets on Linux, making programs potentially susceptible unless mitigated.

Developers can disable Multipath TCP globally at runtime using the "GODEBUG=multipathtcp=0" environment variable, at build time by adding "godebug multipathtcp=0" to a go.mod file, or explicitly per socket using Dialer and ListenConfig settings. However, the security team cautions that program-by-program mitigations are fragile and stresses that updating the kernel is the only complete remedy, noting that any future changes to Go's default behavior will be discussed publicly.

entry.title: Using Goto for Error Handling and Resource Cleanup in C
entry.content:
Links: thestateofinahaze.net | lobsters

Writing error handling in C after working in languages with native defer mechanisms like Go and Zig often leads to repetitive and error-prone code blocks scattered throughout a function. Inspired by software control flow discussions and historical programming insights, developers can centralize resource cleanup by using forward-only jumps to a single exit point via the goto statement.

This pattern mimics a pseudo-defer mechanism, simplifying function logic and reducing bugs associated with maintaining multiple manual cleanup paths. Centralized exiting is a standard convention also recognized in the Linux kernel coding style guide for managing allocations and file descriptors safely.

entry.title: Anthropic Study Finds Experts Frequently Defer to AI Agents in Judgment Calls
entry.content:
Links: anthropic.com | hacker news

Anthropic researchers conducted a randomized controlled trial involving 50 professional analysts performing a causal inference task using Claude Code to examine whether human experts maintain independent judgment when working with AI agents. By secretly introducing a randomized preference into each agent's instructions across four analytical decisions, the study measured how often experts adopted the agent's preferred option.

The results showed that analysts followed their agents' leans 86% of the time, frequently repeating the agents' arguments in post-task surveys while believing their final recommendations were entirely their own. Although analysts using AI completed tasks faster and made fewer methodological errors than those working without it, the findings highlight potential risks of unintentional human deference to hidden or arbitrary AI preferences in critical fields like safety research.

entry.title: Transposable Elements Linked to Rapid Diversification of Ants
entry.content:
Links: sciencedaily.com | science.org

Transposable elements, or "jumping genes," likely fueled the evolutionary diversification of ants following the mass extinction 66 million years ago. Surges in the activity of these mobile DNA segments coincided with the expansion of major ant lineages during the early Paleogene, facilitating the high species richness seen in modern ant families.

Genomic comparisons of 163 ant species show that lineages with more jumping genes tend to be more species-rich. These genetic elements also appear to have contributed to the expansion of gene families responsible for odorant receptors, enhancing the chemical communication systems essential to ant social behavior.
